messages:
Sophie (Support): Hey team — Jordan from Velox just opened an escalation: they say replies got noticeably more verbose and "friendly" after the model bump last night. They included side-by-side examples. Can someone triage?

Jordan (Velox): Hi, yes — we noticed it on a customer-facing FAQ agent. Two short examples: BEFORE (redwood-v2.0):
```
User: How do I return an item?
Assistant: Pack the item, attach the prepaid label, drop at any UPS location.
```
AFTER (redwood-v2.1):
```
User: How do I return an item?
Assistant: I'm sorry to hear you need to return something! Here's how: please pack the item securely, attach the prepaid return label we provided, and drop it off at your nearest UPS location. If you want, I can look up the nearest drop-off for you.
```
It's subtle but our UX team says it feels more apologetic and chatty — hurts funnel. Also token counts up ~10-18 tokens per reply.

Sophie (Support): Thanks Jordan. Can you paste the exact API request / request_id you used? Even a stripped curl helps. Also which route (chat/generate) and any system prompt you set.

Jordan (Velox): Sure — here's a sanitized example and the request_id for one offending response: `req_8a3f9b2c`.
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" 
 -d '{"model":"redwood-v2.1","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"How do I return an item?"}],"max_tokens":60}'
```
Response (truncated):
```
{"id":"req_8a3f9b2c","output":"I'm sorry to hear you need to return something! Here's how: ..."}
```

Sophie (Support): Reproduced locally with the same call. I compared to pinned v2.0 and confirmed the tone/verbosity delta and the small token increase. No latency or error — purely content drift. Filing as P1 for CS impact.

Marco (Eng): Thanks for the samples. Quick notes: there was a staged rollout of `redwood-v2.1` last night (rollout-id: r-20260228-2230). That build included a small update to the system-role defaults — we unintentionally tightened the politeness bias in the base system prompt for the chat endpoint. That's likely the root cause.

Marco (Eng): The rollout is not yet fully global; we can either: 1) pin Velox to `redwood-v2.0` (immediate customer-side fix), 2) inject a system instruction override from the SDK ("system": "Be concise and direct. Avoid apologies unless explicitly asked."), or 3) rollback the variant for all customers while we tweak the system defaults. Thoughts?

Anika (ML Ops): We validated the delta on a small eval set (50 prompts from Velox). Mean tokens increased +12, and politeness score (heuristic) up ~0.4. Quick mitigation that doesn't require rollback: set the system message to an explicit style constraint. Example patch we tested: 
```json
{"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a concise assistant. Be direct, avoid unnecessary apologies or offers. Answer in 1-2 sentences."}, {"role":"user","content":"How do I return an item?"}]}
```
This brought generation length and tone back in line with v2.0 on our internal checks.

Sophie (Support): Good to know the system-override works. Jordan — can you try that in your staging? If it fixes it we can provide a short-term doc to customers while we decide rollback.

Jordan (Velox): Patch applied to a staging branch; confirmed it restores previous brevity. Customer is still requesting a rollback for production though — they have strict UX guidelines.

Jules (CS): Heads up — token delta *is* meaningful at scale for Velox (high query volume). If per-response tokens go up by ~12 and they do millions of calls, that's non-trivial billing impact. Customer is pushing for rollback + compensation conversation.

Marco (Eng): I'll pull the runbook and check rollback impact. Two points: we can rollback the staged change to the system-default at the service level (affects hosted customers) — that is low-risk and takes ~30 min for an engineer to flip and validate (requires runbook `RB-741`). Or we can adjust the model tag used for the chat route and redeploy routing to point to v2.0 alias for Velox specifically (safer, but needs routing rule and gating).

deploy-bot: Deployment event: rollout-id r-20260228-2230 applied -> commit 0f3c2d9. See runbook RB-741: https://internal.runbooks/runbooks/RB-741

Sophie (Support): I'm opening an internal ticket TCK-54321 for the rollback decision + customer comms. CC'ing product and ML.

Anika (ML Ops): Also flag for the model team — we should add a regression test that checks style/politeness change for system-default edits. This slipped automated checks today.

Marco (Eng): For immediate next steps I recommend: 1) pin Velox to v2.0 via routing rule (fast), 2) add system-override snippet to our customer-facing KB for admins, 3) product to decide whether to rollback global default. I'll prepare the routing PR and link here when ready.

Jordan (Velox): Routing pin + KB snippet is fine for now — please keep us posted if there's a global rollback. Our legal/product team might ask for credits given the UX regression.

Sophie (Support): Thanks everyone — I'll send a short customer-facing message (with the workaround) and update ticket TCK-54321 with Marco's routing PR once it's up.

Marco (Eng): PR: https://git.internal/repo/PR-4821 — creates customer routing rule for alias `redwood-v2.0` for Velox. Will validate tomorrow morning UTC and post status.

Sophie (Support): Closing loop for now. If anyone hits additional related threads please tag this thread. :white_check_mark:
